intro: Armenia has been stripped of voting rights in the CSTO over unpaid dues, while the death of an opposition mayoral candidate in detention has sparked protests and debate. Prime Minister Pashinyan held meetings with the leaders of Türkiye and Iran in Antalya.

topics.title: Armenia loses CSTO voting rights over unpaid dues
topics.text: Multiple sources report that Armenia has been deprived of voting rights in the Russian-led CSTO due to unpaid membership fees. The Kremlin and CSTO officials confirmed the measure, which also bars Armenia from appointing representatives to senior posts, and outlined conditions for restoring participation.

topics.title: Opposition candidate dies in custody, prompting protests
topics.text: Opposition mayoral candidate Arsen Gevorgyan died in prison, leading to demonstrations outside the EU Delegation in Yerevan. Lawyers allege the penitentiary service failed to provide medical assistance, while authorities deny the claims and the service released a chronology of events.

topics.title: Pashinyan meets Erdoğan and Pezeshkian in Antalya
topics.text: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan held separate meetings with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the COP31 Leaders' Summit. Discussions focused on Armenia-Türkiye normalization, regional cooperation, and expanding bilateral ties with Iran.

topics.title: Armenia and Finland discuss trade cooperation
topics.text: Officials from Armenia and Finland held talks on developing trade, economic, and investment cooperation. The discussions covered current trade volumes and potential areas for expanding bilateral economic relations.

topics.title: Armenian finance minister addresses economic outlook
topics.text: The finance minister stated that difficulties exporting agricultural products to Russia do not significantly impact the state budget and denied a direct link between possible EAEU membership suspension and declining remittances. The 2027 budget draft envisages a 57 billion dram increase in capital expenditures.

topics.title: Former security chief criticizes EU membership bid
topics.text: Former National Security Service director Artur Vanetsyan described Armenia's EU membership ambitions as an illusion and warned of deeper dependence on Russia. Meanwhile, Ankara signaled readiness to open the Armenia-Türkiye border once a peace deal with Azerbaijan is reached.
